extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for language modeling constructed from Wikipedia articles, available in two sizes: WikiText-2 and WikiText-103.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity; Caiming Xiong; James Bradbury; Richard Socher
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by selecting Wikipedia articles meeting Good or Featured article criteria, extracting their text via the Wikipedia API, and removing list-heavy sections and minor HTML leakage.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Text extracted from Wikipedia articles that fit the Good or Featured article criteria.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: After extraction, list-heavy sections and minor HTML leakage were removed; mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with formula tokens; normalization and tokenization were performed with the Moses tokenizer augmented to split numbers; vocabulary was built by discarding words with count below 3 and mapping out-of-vocabulary words to the unk token.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Wikipedia editors had reviewed the selected Good and Featured articles, which were considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper motivates WikiText by stating that Penn Treebank is unrealistic because it is lowercased, stripped of punctuation, and limited to a 10k-word vocabulary, making it problematic for modeling rare words and real language use.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmark dataset for language modeling, including evaluation of long-range dependencies, realistic vocabularies, and handling of rare words.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We selected articles only fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia. The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API. Once extracted, specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Other minor bugs, such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML, were also removed.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We selected articles only fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia. The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Hence, we constructed a language modeling dataset using text extracted from Wikipedia and will make this available to the community. We selected articles only fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Once extracted, specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Other minor bugs, such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML, were also removed. Mathematical formulae and L ATEX code, were replaced with hformulaitokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), slightly augmented to further split numbers (8,600 !8 @,@ 600) and with some additional minor fixes. Following Chelba et al. (2013) a vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3. Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the hunkitoken, also a part of the vocabulary.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: These articles have been reviewed by humans and are considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007)

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: While the processed version of the PTB above has been frequently used for language modeling, it has many limitations. The tokens in PTB are all lower case, stripped of any punctuation, and limited to a vocabulary of only 10k words. These limitations mean that the PTB is unrealistic for real language use, especially when far larger vocabularies with many rare words are involved.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: In order to evaluate how well language models can exploit longer contexts and deal with more realistic vocabularies and larger corpora we also introduce the freely available WikiText corpus. We have also motivated the need to move from Penn Treebank to a new language modeling dataset for long range dependencies, providing WikiText-2 and WikiText-103 as potential options.
